say: I've not eaten in {days} days.
There was nothing on our table again. {days} days now.
My belly's been empty {days} days, {listener}.

same: Nor us. We share whatever turns up.
It's the same in our house. God help us.
comfortable: Come by tonight, there'll be pottage enough for you.
Here, take a few coins. Don't argue.
other: Go to the church. They're giving alms.
Ask your kin, surely someone can spare a loaf.

say: We've had no fire for {days} nights.
The hearth's been cold {days} nights. The little ones shiver.

same: Wood's dear for everyone just now.
We're burning old fence posts ourselves.
other: The woodcutters can't keep up, they say.
Ask a laborer, they'll sell you deadwood cheap.

say: Coins are short. {mouths} mouths and not enough coming in.
I count the purse twice a day and it never grows.
One more bad week and we're done for.

same: I know it. We're scraping by ourselves.
Times are hard for all of us.
comfortable: The rich houses are taking on servants, try there.
If it comes to it, come to me first.
other: The church helps those who ask.
Something will turn up, it always does.

say: My {tool} is broken and I can't afford another. Working by hand is slow going.
No {tool} again. I'm doing half a day's work in a whole day.

smith: Come to the smithy, I'll see what I can do on the price.
I've a {tool} on the bench, nearly done.
other: The smiths are short of iron, they say.
A merchant can fetch one from {town}, for a price.

say: Have you seen the price of {good} now? {price} coins!
The price of {good} has gone up again. {price} a piece.
I paid {price} for {good} this morning. Robbery.

seller: It's what it costs me to make, friend.
other: Everything's dear this season.
If it keeps up I'll go without.

say: The price of {good} is down to {price} this week.
You can get {good} for {price} now. Good time to buy.

seller: Cheap for you, ruin for me.
Can't get a better price than that.
other: About time something got cheaper.
I'll stock up then.

say: The fields are blighted. Hardly anything's coming up.
Worst harvest I've seen. The wheat's rotten in the ear.

farmer: Mine are the same. I don't know how we'll get through.
I've ploughed for twenty years and never seen it so bad.
other: The granary will open its doors, God willing.
The merchants are bringing grain from {town}, at a price.

say: What a harvest! The carts can barely carry it all.
The fields are heavy this year. God is good.

farmer: Aye, but prices will fall through the floor.
We'll eat well, if nothing else.
other: Bread will be cheap for once.
Good news at last.

say: Bandits on the {town} road again. Everything from outside costs more.
Did you hear? They robbed a cart on the road to {town}.

guard: We're doing what we can. More guards would help.
We'll catch them. Mark my words.
other: Where's the watch when you need them?
I'll not travel till they're caught.

say: The mine came down. Ore will be scarce for a while.
They say three men barely got out of the mine.

other: The smiths will be idle then.
Terrible business. Thank God no one died.

say: This cold! We're burning twice the wood.
I can't remember a winter so bitter.

laborer: Good for my trade, if my hands don't freeze.
Everyone wants wood and there's only so much.
other: Keep the children by the fire.
Wood's dearer by the day.

say: Did you see the fire at the {family} house? They lost nearly everything.
Poor {family}s, burnt out of their stores.

other: We should take them something.
Thank God the watch got there in time.

say: I've given up {from}. I'm a {to} now.
No more {from} for me. I've turned {to}.
I'm a {to} these days. {from} didn't pay.

same_trade: Welcome to it! It's honest work.
other: I hope it serves you better.
A bold move. Good luck to you.

say: I've started work as a {to}. The house needed the coin.
I'm working now, as a {to}.

other: Good for you. It's hard at first.
Your family must be proud.

say: I've gone into service with the {family} household.
I'm a servant at the {family} house now. Steady wage, at least.

other: Better than going hungry.
Are they good masters?

say: The town's taken me on as a {office}.
I'm a {office} now, paid by the treasury.

other: A steady wage! You're lucky.
Serve the town well.

say: They let me go from the {family} house. Couldn't pay me any more.
I'm out of service. The {family}s fell on hard times.

other: You'll find something.
That's a blow. What will you do?

say: My {relation} {name} died. Starved, in the end.
We buried {name} this week. My {relation}.

kin: I loved {name} too. We'll remember them.
other: God rest them. I'm so sorry.
If there's anything I can do...

say: If not for {giver}, we'd have gone without.
{giver} helped us this week. I won't forget it.

other: There's still kindness in this town.
Pass it on when you can.

say: I gave a little to the {family}s. They had nothing.
Saw the {family} children going hungry. Couldn't stand it.

other: That was good of you.
God sees these things.

say: My {relation} {name} helped us out this week.
Family came through. {name} sent coins.

other: That's what family's for.
You're lucky to have them.

say: We live with {name} now. They took us in.
After everything, {name} gave us a home.

other: God bless them for it.
You're in good hands.

say: My {tool} snapped this morning.
Finally wore my {tool} out. Need a new one.

smith: Bring it to me, I'll have a new one by tomorrow.
Iron's dear, but I'll make you one.
other: That'll cost you.
Try the smithy, or a merchant.

say: Good week. Sold all my {good} and then some.
Business is good. I made {gain} coins this week.

envious: Some of us aren't so lucky.
Leave a bit for the rest of us!
other: Glad to hear it.
You've earned it.

say: Bad week. I'm {loss} coins down.
Couldn't sell a thing this week.

other: Next week will be better.
It's the same everywhere.

say: If I can put by enough, I'll take up {trade}. They do well.
I've been thinking of taking up {trade}. There's money in it.

same_trade: There's room for one more, I suppose.
other: Go on, you'd be good at it.
Mind you don't lose your shirt.

say: {child} turns twelve soon. They can start as an apprentice.
{child} is growing fast. Soon they'll bring in a wage.

other: They grow up so quick.
A good child, that one.

say: Times are good. I'm thinking of taking on a servant.
We've put a little by at last. Maybe a bigger house one day.

other: You've worked for it.
God has been kind to you.

pairs: Let's hope it stays that way.
Everyone's out buying before prices go up.
Did you hear the bells at dawn?
My back aches from the work.
Aye, make the most of it.
